query: Why do some travel expenses get declined, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Derivable from the ci field for hardware/cloud rows. But the query is about travel expense declines, and the source text describes hardware/asset procurement, not travel; the category adds only weak leverage. Groundedness is undermined by mislabeling: 'Dell OptiPlex 7070 Desktop' is labeled hardware_laptop, contradicting the source ci.

per_column.name: procurement_urgency
per_column.rationale: A travel_related vs standard split could help the query, but 'urgency' is not stated anywhere in the source text; the values appear to be an invented/relabeled travel flag rather than a grounded reading. Contradicts its own name (urgency) with travel_related values.

per_column.name: expense_categorization_clarity
per_column.rationale: Clarity of purpose is a plausibly useful axis for why an expense is declined, but the sampled short_descriptions all yield clear_purpose, so the value is a defensible reading yet near-constant in evidence and partly subjective.

per_column.name: travel_intent_explicit
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to a travel-expense query and gives a clean grouping axis. Sampled rows (hardware/cloud) are correctly marked false, consistent with the source text. Reasonable inference from description keywords.

per_column.name: processing_lag
per_column.rationale: Timing could relate to declines, but only processed_date is present; without an opened_at/reference in the sampled text, 'fast_track'/'delayed' buckets are unwarranted specifics. Sample with only processed_date=2023-07-21 is labeled 'delayed' with no basis shown; nan row correctly Unknown.

per_column.name: department_expense_pattern
per_column.rationale: Values mirror the existing 'department' original column (a mere restatement/relabel), so it adds little new analytical leverage. Values themselves are grounded in the department field.

per_column.name: asset_value_tier
per_column.rationale: Value tier could plausibly drive declines and is derivable from amount. But tiers appear inconsistent with any stated thresholds; 'AWS EC2 Instance' as high_value is an assertion not supported by the sampled source text (no amount shown), suggesting invented tiering.

per_column.name: user_submission_frequency
per_column.rationale: Submitter frequency could be a useful factor, but it requires cross-row aggregation of the user column and the per-row labels ('frequent_submitter', 'rare') are not verifiable from the single-row source text shown and appear asserted without evidence.

judge.rationale: The table is nominally about hardware/asset procurement records, while the query targets travel-expense declines; several columns (travel_intent_explicit, procurement_urgency, expense_categorization_clarity) do address the travel angle and offer real grouping axes, giving moderate usefulness. However, department_expense_pattern largely restates the original department column, and asset-related columns are only tangential to declines. Groundedness is weak: multiple columns assert unwarranted specifics not supported by the source text (misclassified desktop as laptop, unexplained processing_lag buckets, high_value/frequency labels with no visible basis), indicating notable hallucination, though silent rows are handled correctly with Unknown/NULL.
